author: w. m. sanchez
title: Burgess Owens thanks police officers and highlights NASA Artemis visit in recent tweets
text:
Burgess Owens, U.S. Congressman representing Utah’s 4th district since 2021, expressed his appreciation for law enforcement and space exploration, while also addressing education policy in a series of recent posts on his official Twitter account.
On May 12, 2026, Owens acknowledged the contributions of police officers during National Police Week. He stated, “This National Police Week, I am grateful for the brave men and women who wear the badge and run toward danger so the rest of us don’t have to. We see the sacrifice you and your families make to keep Utah safe and prosperous. Thank you.”
Later that day, Owens highlighted his meeting with astronauts from NASA’s Artemis program, noting their historic achievements. In his words: “An honor to have met the incredible TEAM of astronauts from @NASAArtemis. These four individuals have traveled further away from Earth than any humans in HISTORY. What an incredible inspiration and reminder of all we can accomplish when we come together, give our best efforts,” posted on May 12, 2026.
The following day, May 13, 2026, Owens turned his attention to education policy by promoting legislation he supports. He wrote: “Kids should go to school to get an education, not an indoctrination. The CHARLIE Act would stop your taxpayer dollars from being used to promote radical ideologies in the classroom.”
Owens was born in Columbus, Ohio in 1951 and currently resides in Salt Lake City. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Miami in 1974. After replacing Ben McAdams as representative for Utah’s 4th district in 2021, Owens has focused on issues including public safety and educational reform.
